elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'. 'Driver' is a relational role read through the vehicle's controlled motion. Mapping index: 'The driver of a vehicle' maps to the same aggregate.

As in NRS_484B_263_o1: st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'); rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... controlled-access lane ...)'. The entry is the rise of the subject's overlap with region c, the exit the rise of its absence after overlap; kin.speed tells the subject still moves. 'About to' is read by the movement itself.

'that traffic' refers back to these words, so they keep their full qualification here: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; a footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the same controlled-access region c; moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance), with the subject ahead in its frame (rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame', longitudinal component positive).

'traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'); 'that traffic' is the approaching vehicles of a4, so a road user the duty concerns carries both aggregates. The continuing yield is read like the yield (mapping index 'shall yield': kin.speed, rel.contact): while the subject moves, no contact (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)', not a stand-in for a near miss, which a5 and a7 carry). 'continue' places the duty after the entry or exit, read on the clock (kin.time 'instant of observation') through the time since that event.

operationalizations.standard: proximity that constitutes an immediate hazard (the traffic the continuing yield concerns)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision threshold at a centre distance below the collision clearance

operationalizations.standard: until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety
operationalizations.convention: the subject may proceed with reasonable safety once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in a traffic-conflict (closest approach within the time-to-collision threshold below the collision clearance); the continuing duty is read over the merge or diverge that follows the entry or exit, whose duration is the time an acceleration or deceleration lane is run

applicability: The subject (vehicle aggregate) is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), and there is a controlled-access region c whose latest entry or exit by the subject (the latest rise of the subject's overlap with c, or of its non-overlap with c after overlapping it) lies strictly before this observation and no more than p.merge_window before it (Term.sinceRise of that event above zero and at most p.merge_window).
obligation: For every such region c (re-bound with that selection): for every other road user v of the traffic aggregate and of the vehicle aggregate that is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance), whose footprint overlaps c, and in whose frame the subject lies ahead (longitudinal component of rel.bearing from v to the subject positive): the subject and v are not in contact, and it is not the case that their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion
'about to enter or exit' is read by the entry into or exit from the controlled-access region as the source maps it, as in NRS_484B_263_o1

the continuing yield is judged at the observations that follow the entry or exit within the merge window; once that window has run the subject is taken to have merged or diverged, and its later conduct is judged by the following and lane rules, not by this one
'reasonable safety' is read through the same traffic-conflict bound as the immediate hazard: the subject may proceed once no approaching vehicle of that traffic is in such a conflict with it

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered controlled-access region c a short time ago (within p.merge_window, after the entry observation) and keeps moving; vehicle v (traffic and vehicle aggregates) moves on c with the subject ahead of it and their closest approach falls within p.conflict_horizon below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but every vehicle on c is far behind: no closest approach within p.conflict_horizon, no contact.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered c long before, more than p.merge_window ago, and travels within it; v closes from behind.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid (velocities, positions and headings observed, so the closest approach is a conflict), but kin.speed is not observed: whether the subject is still moving and whether v is a moving vehicle approaching it are unknown while the conflict holds.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Within p.merge_window after its entry into c, the subject moves and no other road user is in the scene: the duty binds the subject alone and is met.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's vehicle-state estimates

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic-conflict technique literature (Hyden; FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width

param_proposals.name: p.merge_window
param_proposals.convention: the time an entering or exiting vehicle takes, after coming onto or leaving the controlled-access highway, to complete its merge into or diverge from the highway's traffic: an acceleration or deceleration lane of about 250 m run at about 25 m/s
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book acceleration and deceleration lane lengths
